channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: 'Choose your budget!' shout ULB students rallying on the Solbosch campus
item.description: The organisers said the action was designed to present students with what they described as two opposing visions for society.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 13 - 15 November
item.description: Whether you want to brave the cold for a walking tour or are looking for cosy indoor activities, here are The Brussels Times top picks for this weekend.

item.title: US expresses interest in buying Brussels Minister-President’s €45 million official residence
item.description: The US has expressed interest in purchasing the official residence of Brussels Minister-President Boris Dilliès (MR). The Brussels government plans to sell the building to tackle the region’s budget deficit.

item.title: Deadly shooting near EU Parliament linked to Brussels police officer Nordine's killing
item.description: The men suspected of shooting dead Brussels police officer Nordine El Talbi in Jette in October had allegedly killed a man near the EU Parliament that same evening.

item.title: Man carrying two plastic weapons arrested at Brussels Airport
item.description: A man was arrested at Brussels Airport after entering the departure hall with two plastic weapons.

item.title: Belgium unveils 29 measures to tackle online fraud
item.description: The Belgian Federal Government has announced a new action plan to combat online fraud, introducing 29 measures aimed at preventing phishing.

item.title: Student rooms in Brussels now cost an average €705 a month to rent
item.description: Across Belgium's 10 largest cities, the average rent price is now €600 for the current 2026–2027 academic year; this has increased by €10 in the last year.

item.title: Person armed with weapon arrested in Molenbeek
item.description: The individual was seen on Rue Delaunoy holding a weapon and subsequently entered a property on Chaussée de Gand, according to the police.

item.title: Fewer bin bags on pavements: Brussels Place Jourdan moves rubbish underground
item.description: Jourdan attracts numerous residents, workers and visitors with its terraces and legendary friterie – resulting in specific cleanliness challenges.

item.title: Suspect in Schaerbeek café femicide case released from prison on technicality
item.description: Prosecutors had detained the suspect since December 2024 over the killing of his 36-year-old ex-partner.

item.title: Prince Harry urges EU to put children before social media profit
item.description: His speech coincided with the launch of the "Lost Screen Memorial," an installation honouring children and young people whose deaths were linked to online harm.

item.title: New Brussels drugs commissioner given three months to draft co-ordinating strategy
item.description: Incoming drugs commissioner Miran Scheers has been given three months to draft a strategy for co-ordinating municipalities, police, and federal authorities.

item.title: Brussels Unions to protest austerity measures on Friday 13 November
item.description: Trade unions representing Brussels local and regional authorities will stage a protest on Friday, 13 November.

item.title: Anderlecht Mayor tells US ambassador to 'mind his own business' in synagogue vandalism row
item.description: Anderlecht mayor Fabrice Cumps has dismissed comments by the United States ambassador to Belgium, Bill White, after he visited an Orthodox Jewish synagogue.

item.title: One third of Brussels healthcare facilities overexposed to NO₂
item.description: “It would be a scandal to find cyanide in paracetamol. So why do we accept breathing in nitrogen dioxide at concentrations that are hazardous to health in the vicinity of our hospitals?"

item.title: 'Symbol of submission': Brussels secretary claims to be fired over privately worn headscarf
item.description: A woman has taken the City of Brussels to the labour tribunal, alleging that municipal bosses fired her because she wears an Islamic headscarf outside work.

item.title: 120 take part in ‘Sing/Fuck the Planet’ protest in Brussels
item.description: The protest called for stronger climate justice and more ambitious policy in the run-up to the COP31 conference to be held in Türkiye.

item.title: Young man killed by telehandler in Brussels
item.description: Authorities believe the telehandler had been used by several young people during the night before the incident.

item.title: Infamous Anderlecht drug gang to go to court on Monday
item.description: 45 people are suspected of participating in the Peterbos drug ring.

item.title: US ambassador to Belgium outraged by Brussels synagogue attack
item.description: Bill White visited the synagogue in Anderlecht on Saturday with Israel’s ambassador to Belgium, David Saranga, after the building was targeted in what White called a clear act of antisemitic vandalism.
